newsitem.title: FRANCE: Far-right chief hails absent Joan of Arc statue.
newsitem.headline: Far-right chief hails absent Joan of Arc statue.

text.p: French far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen paid tribute to national heroine Joan of Arc before an empty pedestal on Thursday after her statue was whisked away for repairs to thwart an earlier demonstration.

Le Pen described as "a base political manoeuvre" the decision of former Strasbourg Socialist mayor Catherine Trautmann to remove the statue in April when his National Front (FN) party held a congress in the city. The statue is to be replaced in the autumn.
Trautmann, now France's culture minister, made clear at the time she was exasperated Le Pen had "annexed" Joan of Arc as a symbol for his anti-immigrant movement.
Le Pen, who was in Strasbourg for a closed-door FN meeting, laid a wreath before the statue's pedestal, accompanied by some 40 FN officials and sympathisers.
Joan, a 15th century peasant girl, is best known for leading a campaign to eject the English from France. She was burned at the stake.
